author: Mark Atwood
text:
Filing 'human' because the bead presents three fix candidates without a recommendation, and two of them (private+accessor, newtype wrapper) would REVERSE the workspace policy already documented at /home/mark/PROJECT/crate-jmap/AGENTS.md "Caller contract — wire-key collisions" (lines 292-312):

> Workspace policy is to enforce this contract at the doc / convention layer, not via a wrapper type, because the alternative (an accessor or newtype) would forbid zero-cost passthrough of vendor-namespace dicts and the workspace precedent in 'jmap-types::MethodResponseError.extra' is also a bare 'pub Map'.

That paragraph explicitly addresses bead-concern (1) (direct-mutation access locks out future hardening) — Mark chose pub Map with eyes open. The bead-concern (2) (serde_json major-version coupling) is implicit in the broader workspace pattern but not explicitly called out in AGENTS.md.

Recommendation: accept the lock (candidate 3); strengthen AGENTS.md with one paragraph explicitly noting that 'serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>' couples every consumer to serde_json's major version forever, that this is a known tradeoff, and that the workspace accepts it for consistency with the Sloppy-Value pattern and the rest of the kit's serde_json use.

Rationale for not autonomously applying the recommendation:
- Even the doc-only candidate 3 touches workspace-architectural AGENTS.md and codifies a forever-commitment.
- The bead author wrote this AFTER reading the existing AGENTS.md (the bead body cites the existing policy text) and concluded it's INSUFFICIENT. That's a policy-revisitation question, not a mechanical decision.
- Pre-0.2 is the cheapest time to revisit. If the maintainer wants to harden via candidate 1 or 2 before publishing, the cost is bounded; after 0.2 cuts, it's a major-version-bump cost across 30 crates.

Awaiting maintainer direction on which candidate to apply.
